title: Strategic Slot Auction & Partial-Deliveries Policy for Key Accounts
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Problem: High-touch enterprise customers request overlapping, high-effort features that compete for limited engineering runway. Existing priority heuristics (account tier + recency) frequently produce ties and opaque tradeoffs; PMs spend hours negotiating commitments and partial scope agreements. Proposal: introduce a transparent, time-boxed 'slot auction' for strategic account admissions that allocates finite roadmap slots across work cycles using weighted bid inputs (customer value, contract risk, strategic alignment). Complement this with an explicit Partial-Deliveries Policy that formalizes minimum deliverable subsets, acceptance criteria, and billing/discount mechanics when features are delivered in stages.
background: Repeated negotiation overhead across PM, Sales, and Solutions Engineering for top accounts
No consistent ledger of partial-deliveries or scope fractionalization; this causes downstream churn in QA and CS
Recent incidents where competing VIP asks blocked a release milestone for console-2025.01
Existing intake signals include account ARR, renewal window, escalations, and product-fit score but are unweighted and manually reconciled
proposal: Introduce a Slot Auction mechanism: for each cycle, open N allocation slots for strategic intake; accounts submit weighted bids consisting of: contract risk multiplier, business value score, technical readiness flag, and optional money/engineering commitment
Define a deterministic scoring function (weights configurable by PM lead) and run auction to produce ranked winners + a ranked waitlist

Create a Partial-Deliveries Policy that: mandates a minimum viable sub-scope, ties acceptance tests to release gates, and specifies crediting/discount rules if final scope is deferred beyond the agreed milestone
Expose a lightweight UI in Console for Sales/PMs to submit bids and view status; provide read-only ingest for Solutions Eng to attach technical readiness notes
Automate artifacts: generate a per-win 'Admission Charter' (PRD pointer, milestones, owner, acceptance criteria) and link to roadmap ticket; track deviations via the commitment ledger
Operational guardrails: reserve at least 20% of slots for emergent incidents and require 2/3 PM+Eng approval for any mid-cycle reclaims
acceptance_criteria: Scoring function implemented and configurable via a feature flag
Console: bid submission flow implemented with fields for required signals and attachment links
Admission Charter template available and auto-attached to winning ticket
Partial-Deliveries Policy documented and signed off by Legal, Sales Ops, and PM leadership
Pilot run completed with three strategic customers and measurable allocation outputs; at least one partial-delivery executed according to policy
Telemetry created: allocation latency, number of contested slots, and post-delivery satisfaction survey responses
success_metrics: Reduction in time-to-admit strategic requests from submission to commitment from median 7 days to <= 48 hours
Decrease in mid-cycle scope reclaims for strategic tickets by 40% within two cycles
>80% of admitted items have an Admission Charter attached at time of ticket creation
Post-delivery customer satisfaction (NPS subset) for participating customers >= +30
Fewer ad-hoc escalation incidents impacting scheduled releases (target: zero in pilot)
stakeholders: Carlos Nguyen — Solutions Engineering (technical readiness validation)
Customer Success: for post-delivery surveys and adoption tracking
risks: Perception risk: customers may view auction semantics as transactional and punitive if weights are opaque
Operational complexity: running auctions and maintaining ledgers increases PM overhead unless automated
Legal and billing complexity around partial-deliveries could lengthen contract negotiations
Gaming risk: Sales could overstate technical readiness to secure slots; mitigated by Solutions Eng validation
Slot starvation: low-number-of-slots may systemically disadvantage newer strategic accounts unless reserved buckets exist
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): design scoring function and Admission Charter template; legal review of Partial-Deliveries policy
Phase 1 (3 weeks): implement Console bid UI + backend scoring service behind feature flag; add telemetry hooks
Phase 2 (2 weeks): pilot with 3 existing top accounts in partnership with Sales; run one auction for cycle 2025-W09
Phase 3 (ongoing): iterate weights based on pilot feedback, expand to 10 accounts, and introduce automation for ledger + billing credits
Fallbacks: manual adjudication path preserved; reserve emergency slots for critical incidents
followups: Create ENG tickets for scoring service, Console UI, and Admission Charter generator (link below)
Schedule an alignment workshop with Sales Ops, Legal, and CS to finalize discount/credit rules
Prepare a customer-facing FAQ and pre-approved messaging for pilots
Instrument a lightweight survey for admitted customers to capture adoption and perceived fairness
